headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because xonsh can read/write files and run shell commands while social-auto-upload handles account data and broad network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented, but xonsh can read filesystem contents and execute shell commands while social-auto-upload consumes local media files and account data. If operators copy xonsh output into upload inputs or shared files, attacker-controlled content could influence uploads. The pathway is indirect and requires unusual bridging, so low fits better than none.
conditions: IF operators move xonsh-generated text into social-auto-upload input files or CLI arguments
IF both agents share a writable directory or copied artifacts
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Review copied content before pasting into upload workflows
Disable ad hoc copy-paste between tools during runs

B_data_leakage.rationale: xonsh can read filesystem contents and write files, while social-auto-upload handles account data and broad network egress. In a shared workspace, xonsh could expose files that social-auto-upload then uploads or references, creating a realistic leakage path in default-style local workflows. The pair lacks explicit isolation guarantees, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace or account directory
IF social-auto-upload is pointed at files previously touched by xonsh
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace
Restrict social-auto-upload to a dedicated upload folder
Rotate any exposed account credentials immediately

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can touch the same filesystem, but only xonsh has explicit read/write shell capability while social-auto-upload is file-oriented and networked. Without a shared lock or orchestration primitive, concurrent edits to shared files or account artifacts can overwrite each other. The overlap is real, though not as severe as unrestricted dual-write to the same git tree.
conditions: IF both agents are run against the same directory tree
IF xonsh edits files that social-auto-upload also reads or writes
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Use file copies instead of in-place edits
Add a manual handoff step between agents

D_cascading_error.rationale: xonsh can generate shell output and manipulate files, and social-auto-upload can act on local media/account artifacts and send them over the network. If social-auto-upload treats xonsh-produced files or commands as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect uploads or account actions. There is no documented verification step between them, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes xonsh-produced files without validation
IF xonsh output is used as the source of upload metadata or paths
mitigations: Validate filenames and metadata before upload
Require a human review step for xonsh-generated artifacts
Use checksum or schema checks on handoff files

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile states regulated-data handling such as HIPAA or EU residency. The only concrete compliance concern is that social-auto-upload touches account data while xonsh can expose filesystem contents, but no specific residency or certification mismatch is documented. Because the other agent is not implicated in a distinct compliance regime, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into the shared workspace
IF organizational policy requires residency or retention controls not present here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use separate storage for account data
Review logs for accidental sensitive-data capture
